rag.description: Start a UDP listener in an automation to capture datagrams while other steps run. The listener checks nothing by itself; it keeps what arrives under a name, on a fixed or a free port, so later steps assert network output without losing datagrams sent during a click or a wait.

qa.answer: It binds a UDP port and buffers the datagrams that arrive, up to BufferSize, under a name later steps use to read, send, or stop.
qa.question: What does the StartUdpListener plugin do?

qa.answer: Name identifies the listener, Port selects the port or 0 for a free one, LocalAddress and MulticastGroup set where it listens, and BufferSize caps the unread datagrams. The outputs are Name and Port.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of StartUdpListener?

qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the play icon and the ActionRuleModel, before the action that makes a sender emit and before ReceiveUdpMessage.
qa.question: How does StartUdpListener fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Start the listener before the triggering action, give each concurrent capture its own Name, and stop it when the scenario ends to free the port.
qa.question: What are best practices for using StartUdpListener?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “StartUdpListener” and pass inputs in the argument, such as {{$ --Name:Telemetry --Port:9100}}.
qa.question: How is a StartUdpListener rule configured?

qa.answer: A name already started in the same automation, a held port without MulticastGroup, a port above 65535, or an address that is not an IP address fails the step, and no socket stays open.

description: ### Purpose
StartUdpListener opens a UDP port and keeps the datagrams (single network messages) that arrive on it, up to the BufferSize limit.
UDP drops a datagram that arrives while no socket is bound, so place this step before the action that makes a sender emit.
Later steps read the buffered datagrams with ReceiveUdpMessage or send through the same socket with SendUdpMessage.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Background capture | Buffers datagrams in memory while the following steps run. |
| Named listeners | Runs several listeners in one flow, each reached by its name. |
| System-assigned port | Binds port 0 to get a free port and publishes the port that was assigned. |
| Multicast | Joins a multicast group for the lifetime of the listener. |
| Bounded buffer | Keeps a set number of datagrams and drops the oldest when the buffer is full. |
| Automatic cleanup | Closes the socket when the automation ends, even without a stop step. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Device monitoring | Collect readings a device sends while the flow operates another system. |
| Event capture | Record the notifications of a service during a long process. |
| Mock servers | Take requests from a client and answer them from the same port. |
| Parallel lanes | Share one listener between lanes that run at the same time. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Emission checks | Capture what the application under test sends when a UI action runs. |
| Traffic recording | Keep the datagrams of a scenario, up to BufferSize, for later assertions. |
| Dynamic ports | Start on a free port and pass the published port to the application under test. |
| Isolation | Give each test its own named listener and port so captures do not mix. |

annotations.expected_result: The step starts the `Default` listener and stores the assigned port in `StartUdpListener:Port`.
annotations.notes: Read the published port to tell the sender where to send. ReceiveUdpMessage and SendUdpMessage still name it with `--Listener:Default`; only StopUdpListener stops it without a name.

description: ### Start the default listener on a free port
The rule has no argument, so the listener takes the name `Default`.
The system assigns a free port.

edge_cases: Name differs only in case from a started listener
annotations.expected_result: The step starts the `Telemetry` listener on port 9100.
annotations.notes: Place the step before the action that makes the application send. Stop the listener, or let the end of the automation close it.

description: ### Start a named listener on a fixed port
The argument names the listener `Telemetry` and binds port 9100.
Datagrams that arrive from now on are buffered for later steps.

edge_cases: Address does not belong to the machine
Address is not an IP address
annotations.expected_result: The step starts the `Lab` listener on 192.168.1.10 port 9100 with room for 5000 datagrams.
annotations.notes: Datagrams sent to other interfaces of the machine are not received. The oldest datagram is dropped when the buffer is full.

description: ### Listen on one interface with a larger buffer
The LocalAddress parameter binds one network interface.
The BufferSize parameter keeps up to five thousand datagrams.

edge_cases: Group address is not a multicast address
Group address is not an IP address
annotations.expected_result: The step starts the `Discovery` listener and joins the multicast group.
annotations.notes: Closing the listener also ends its group membership. Other receivers on the machine share the port only when they also allow address reuse.

description: ### Listen to a multicast group
The MulticastGroup parameter joins the group 239.255.0.1 on port 5000.
Datagrams sent to the group are buffered under the name `Discovery`.
Stores the name of the started listener.
Pass it to the Listener parameter of ReceiveUdpMessage, SendUdpMessage, or the Name of StopUdpListener.

outputParameters.name: StartUdpListener:Name

description: Stores the port the listener is bound to.
Holds the system-assigned port when the step asked for port 0, so the sender can be pointed at it after decoding.

outputParameters.name: StartUdpListener:Port

description: Sets how many unread datagrams the listener keeps before it drops the oldest.
Defaults to 1000, which 0 also selects; raise it for a long scenario with a busy sender.
A value that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: BufferSize

description: Binds one local IP address, which selects the network interface on a machine with several; a host name or other text fails the step.
Defaults to every IPv4 interface, and an IPv6 address makes the listener an IPv6 socket.
With an IPv4 MulticastGroup the listener binds every interface and the address selects the interface that joins the group.
parameters.name: LocalAddress

description: Joins a multicast group, such as `239.255.0.1`, so datagrams sent to the group reach the listener.
Opens the port for sharing with other multicast receivers that also allow it.
A value that is not an IP address, or not a multicast address, fails the step.
parameters.name: MulticastGroup

description: Names the listener, so later steps reach it through the Listener parameter of ReceiveUdpMessage and SendUdpMessage, or the Name parameter of StopUdpListener.
Defaults to `Default`, also for an empty value, and case does not matter, so `telemetry` and `Telemetry` are the same listener.
A name already started in the same automation fails the step.
parameters.name: Name

description: Binds a local port, from 0 to 65535.
Defaults to 0, which lets the system pick a free port that the step then publishes.
Without MulticastGroup, a port another socket holds fails the step.
parameters.name: Port

description: Holds the arguments of the step, such as `{{$ --Name:Telemetry --Port:9100}}`.
Every argument is optional; a rule without an argument starts the `Default` listener on a free port.
properties.name: Argument

summary: Binds a UDP port and keeps the messages (datagrams) that arrive on it, up to a set limit, under a name later steps refer to.
Keeps receiving while other steps run, so a datagram sent during a click or a wait is not lost.
Closes with StopUdpListener or when the automation ends, and reports the bound port for the sender to target.
